arxiv-2111-11540.title: High power vacuum ultraviolet source based on gasdynamic ECR plasma
arxiv-2111-11540.creator: R. L. Lapin, V. A. Skalyga, S. V. Golubev, I. V. Izotov, S. V. Razin, O. Tarvainen
arxiv-2111-11540.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by R. L. Lapin, V. A. Skalyga, S. V. Golubev, I. V. Izotov, S. V. Razin, O. Tarvainen. We report experimental results of vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) emission from the plasma of an electron cyclotron resonance (ECR) discharge in hydrogen, sustained by powerful millimeter-wavelength radiation of a gyrotron.

arxiv-2206-00783.title: Core-periphery Models for Hypergraphs Conference: Proceedings of the 28th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining; August 14–18, 2022; Washington, DC, USA Proceedings of the 28th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD ’22), August 14–18, 2022, Washingt
arxiv-2206-00783.creator: Marios Papachristou, Jon Kleinberg
arxiv-2206-00783.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Marios Papachristou, Jon Kleinberg. We introduce a random hypergraph model for core-periphery structure. By leveraging our model’s sufficient statistics, we develop a novel statistical inference algorithm that is able to scale to large hypergraphs with runtime that is practically linear wrt. the number of nodes in the graph after a preprocessing step that is almost linear in the number of hyperedges, as well as a scalable sampling algorithm.

arxiv-2206-09937.title: The norm of the resolvent of the Volterra operator
arxiv-2206-09937.creator: Thomas Ransford
arxiv-2206-09937.description: Abstract . In this expository note, we compute the exact value of the norm of the resolvent of the Volterra operator. 1. Introduction Let V:L^{2}[0,1]\to L^{2}[0,1] be the Volterra operator, defined by Vf(x):=\int_{0}^{x}f(t)\,dt. It is well known that V is a compact quasi-nilpotent operator, and that its adjoint is given by V^{*}f(x)=\int_{x}^{1}f(t)\,dt.

arxiv-2307-00655.title: Revisiting Arnold’s topological proof of the Morse index theorem
arxiv-2307-00655.creator: Eduardo V. Sodré
arxiv-2307-00655.description: Abstract . We give an exposition of the Morse Index Theorem in the Riemannian case in terms of the Maslov index, following and expanding upon Arnold’s seminal paper. We emphasize the symplectic arguments in the proof and aim to be as self-contained as possible. 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification 58E10 (Primary), 53D12 (Secondary) 1.

arxiv-2402-11013.title: Prompt Black Hole Formation in Binary Neutron Star Mergers Preprint: APCTP Pre2024 - 006
arxiv-2402-11013.creator: Christian Ecker, Konrad Topolski, Matti Järvinen, Alina Stehr
arxiv-2402-11013.description: Abstract We carry out an in-depth analysis of the prompt-collapse behaviour of binary neutron star (BNS) mergers. To this end, we perform more than 80 80 general relativistic BNS merger simulations using a family of realistic Equations of State (EOS) with different stiffness, which feature a first order deconfinement phase transition between hadronic and quark matter.

arxiv-2403-01255.title: Automatic Speech Recognition using Advanced Deep Learning Approaches: A survey
arxiv-2403-01255.creator: Hamza Kheddarcor1, Mustapha Hemis, Yassine Himeur
arxiv-2403-01255.description: Abstract Recent advancements in deep learning (DL) have posed a significant challenge for automatic speech recognition (ASR). ASR relies on extensive training datasets, including confidential ones, and demands substantial computational and storage resources. Enabling adaptive systems improves ASR performance in dynamic environments. DL techniques assume training and testing data originate from the same domain, which is not always true.

arxiv-2406-13275.title: Enhancing Automated Audio Captioning via Large Language Models with Optimized Audio Encoding Thanks: ∗ Corresponding author. Thanks: ♯ Equal contribution.
arxiv-2406-13275.creator: Jizhong Liu, Gang Li, Junbo Zhang, Heinrich Dinkel, Yongqing Wang, Zhiyong Yan, Yujun Wang, Bin Wang
arxiv-2406-13275.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jizhong Liu, Gang Li, Junbo Zhang, Heinrich Dinkel, Yongqing Wang, Zhiyong Yan, Yujun Wang, Bin Wang. Automated audio captioning (AAC) is an audio-to-text task to describe audio contents in natural language. Recently, the advancements in large language models (LLMs), with improvements in training approaches for audio encoders, have opened up possibilities for improving AAC.

arxiv-2408-15424.title: Asim Gangopadhyaya
arxiv-2408-15424.description: Abstract Semiclassical methods are essential in analyzing quantum mechanical systems. Although they generally produce approximate results, relatively rare potentials exist for which these methods are exact. Such intriguing potentials serve as crucial test cases for semiclassical approximations. Recent research has demonstrated a deep connection between supersymmetric quantum mechanics and the exactness of semiclassical methods.

arxiv-2412-09503.title: AdS amplitudes as CFT correlators
arxiv-2412-09503.creator: Máximo Bañados, Ernesto Bianchi, Iván Muñoz, Kostas Skenderis
arxiv-2412-09503.description: Abstract We show that AdS amplitudes are CFT correlators to all orders in the loop expansion by showing that they obey the conformal Ward identities. In particular, we provide explicit formulas for the constants and functions of cross-ratios that determine the CFT correlators in terms of bulk data.

arxiv-2504-17939.title: A computational model of infant sensorimotor exploration in the mobile paradigm
arxiv-2504-17939.creator: Josua Spisak, Sergiu Tcaci Popescu, Stefan Wermter, Matej Hoffmann, J. Kevin O’Regan
arxiv-2504-17939.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Josua Spisak, Sergiu Tcaci Popescu, Stefan Wermter, Matej Hoffmann, J. Kevin O’Regan. We present a computational model of the mechanisms that may determine infant behavior in the ‘‘mobile paradigm’’. This paradigm has been used in developmental psychology to explore how infants learn the sensory effects of their actions. In this paradigm, a mobile (an articulated and movable object hanging above an infant’s crib) is connected to one of the infant’s limbs, prompting the infant to preferentially move that ‘‘connected’’ limb.

arxiv-2507-20134.title: Gauge fields in the presence of the electroweak bubble wall
arxiv-2507-20134.creator: Takahiro Kubota
arxiv-2507-20134.description: Abstract The gauge field theory of the standard electroweak model in the presence of the electroweak bubble wall is investigated, with an eye toward its applications to microscopic phenomena which are supposed to have occurred during the phase transition in the early universe.

pmc-11445903.title: Polypharmacy and potentially inappropriate medicine use in older adults with cancer: a multicenter cross-sectional study in Northwest Ethiopia oncologic centers
pmc-11445903.creator: Samuel Agegnew Wondm, Tilaye Arega Moges, Samuel Berihun Dagnew, Fisseha Nigussie Dagnew, Tirsit Ketsela Zeleke, Rahel Belete Abebe, Endalamaw Aschale Mihrete, Fasil Bayafers Tamene
pmc-11445903.description: BackgroundMost patients with cancer have comorbid conditions that necessitate advanced medical treatment. Polypharmacy (PP) and potentially inappropriate medicine (PIM) use is common among older adult patients with cancer. Not much research has been conducted on PP and PIM use among older adult patients with cancer in Ethiopian oncology centers.

pmc-11504235.title: Patient and Community Perspectives on Antibiotics and Antimicrobial Resistance: Fertile Grounds for Antimicrobial Stewardship
pmc-11504235.creator: Anthony Baffoe-Bonnie, Mandy Swann, Carter Gottschalk, Brent Brewer, Nathan Everson
pmc-11504235.description: Background: Antimicrobial resistance is a serious public health threat. Overuse of antibiotics leads to the development and spread of antibiotic resistant pathogens. Antibiotics are also responsible for a high percentage of emergency department visits for adverse drug events. Despite this, ambulatory and urgent care providers often cite patient expectations as a reason for inappropriate antibiotic prescribing practices.

pmc-11728169.title: Functional Mechanical Behavior and Biocompatible Characteristics of Graphene-Coated Cardiovascular Stents
pmc-11728169.creator: Łukasz Wasyluk, Dariusz Hreniak, Vitalii Boiko, Beata Sobieszczańska, Emanuela Bologna, Massimiliano Zingales, Robert Pasławski, Jacek Arkowski, Przemysław Sareło, Magdalena Wawrzyńska, Liviu Duta
pmc-11728169.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) is a treatment method that involves reopening narrowed arteries with a balloon catheter that delivers a cylindrical, mesh-shaped implant device to the site of the stenosis. Currently, by applying a coating to a bare metal stent (BMS) surface to improve biocompatibility, the main risks after PCI, such as restenosis and thrombosis, are reduced while maintaining the basic requirements for the mechanical behavior of the stent itself.

pmc-12571207.title: Integrated Microfluidic Platform for Longitudinal Imaging, Functional Assays, and Downstream Proteomics in C. elegans
pmc-12571207.creator: Noa Marchoom‐Bura, Shira Zelikman, David Morgenstern, Yishi Levin, Efrat Barbiro‐Michaely, Ehud Banin, Sivan Henis‐Korenblit, Doron Gerber
pmc-12571207.description: Caenorhabditis elegans is a widely used model organism in developmental biology, neurobiology, and host‐pathogen research. However, existing approaches for long‐term, high‐content imaging of individual worms are constrained by stress‐inducing immobilization and fragmented observational workflows. Here, a microfluidic platform is introduced that enables continuous, high‐resolution imaging of individual C.

pmc-12722454.title: Worldwide distribution of human pythosis and biological characteristics of a Pythium insidiosum strain susceptible to antibiotics from China: a dual-scale study
pmc-12722454.creator: Xiaoyun Liu, Qiuyue Diao, Mingliang Li, Yuting Yang, Jiayin Liang, Zehua Cui, Haiyan Zhang, Huiling He, Jiabao Huang, Hao Ren, Fengli Zhou, Tijiang Shan, Xiaopin Liao, Jian Sun, Kouxing Zhang
pmc-12722454.description: IntroductionPythiosis, caused by Pythium insidiosum (P. insidiosum), is an emerging disease with high mortality and morbidity. Despite its clinical severity and geographical strain variations, diagnostic and treatment challenges persist.Materials and methodsWe queried PubMed and Google Scholar for “P. insidiosum” and “pythiosis,” 1084 human pythiosis cases to generate a corresponding distribution map.

pmc-13298044.title: Extended Divergence on a Foliation by Continuous-Type Escort Distributions
pmc-13298044.creator: Keiko Uohashi
pmc-13298044.description: From an information geometric perspective, this study considers a natural foliation of dualistic structures associated with escort distributions of exponential families. We propose an extended divergence on this foliation by continuous-type escort distributions. Specifically, we investigate the foliation formed by escort distributions to analyze the transition of q-parameters, rather than relying on a fixed parameter.

pmc-13402412.title: Multidrug-resistant organisms on in-use medical textiles in a Shanghai tertiary hospital: surveillance and genomic characterization
pmc-13402412.creator: Chunyan Li, Jing Zhang, Lulu Gao, Yue Li, Yilun Zhou, Bin Wang, Na Ji, Shan Wang, Fei Wang, Liang Tian
pmc-13402412.description: BackgroundMedical textiles are frequently handled in healthcare settings and may serve as reservoirs for multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs). This study investigated bacterial contamination, MDRO prevalence and genomic characteristics of MDRO isolates recovered from medical textiles in a tertiary hospital.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted between April and August 2024.

pmc-13646003.title: An ethical defense of safer supply
pmc-13646003.creator: Arthur Krieger
pmc-13646003.description: Safer supply is a medical form of harm reduction in which a patient is prescribed a drug to which they are addicted. Despite ample high-quality evidence that it is a safe and effective last-line treatment for severe, treatment-refractory substance use disorders, safer supply is not widely used or advocated.

pmc-13685046.title: Resorcinol in Dermatology: Reassessing a Legacy Topical Therapy for Contemporary Clinical Use
pmc-13685046.creator: Omar Raheel, Natalie Asemi, Aarushi Gulati, Victoria McGuirt, Maham Usmani, Steven R Feldman
pmc-13685046.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundResorcinol is a phenolic topical agent with a long history in dermatology, but its role in contemporary practice has narrowed substantially. This review summarizes the mechanism, formulation considerations, clinical applications, safety profile, and future relevance of topical resorcinol.SummaryResorcinol has keratolytic, antiseptic, antifungal, anti-inflammatory, and tyrosinase-inhibitory properties that support its use in acne, hidradenitis suppurativa, chemical peels, hyperkeratotic disorders, and pigmentary conditions. Despite historical use in acne, current evidence and guideline support are limited, and resorcinol remains largely absent from routine acne management.
